oncall-bot: ALERT: GPU pool 'g-pool-1' queue > 25k requests, avg latency spike, autoscaler error 422. Throttles observed on /v1/generate. Severity: P1. Incident channel: #incidents. Paging maya (oncall) and eng-runtime.
maya (oncall): I'm on it. Seeing sustained queue growth starting ~08:47 UTC. Autoscaler logs show repeated 'scale limit reached' and API returning 429 for scale requests. Link to dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/g-pool-1
eric (eng-runtime): I see the autoscaler attempted 3 times to add nodes but got back "quota_exceeded" from cloud provider at 08:49. However, the root-cause metric: per-GPU throughput dropped ~40% around 08:44, while qps held steady => more requests stayed queued. Any recent runtime changes rolled out? @raj @sophie
raj (eng-ml): We rolled a batching/caching tweak in canary at 08:30 that changed continuous batching behavior: default max_batch_latency bumped from 10ms -> 50ms and prefix cache key normalization changed (strip_user_id flag turned off). Canary looked ok on small traffic though. Could be related.
sophie (eng-sre): Correlating logs: prefix_cache.miss_rate jumped 8x at 08:44. Concurrently, avg batch size dropped from 18 tokens to 6 tokens — fewer tokens batched per request, so throughput per GPU down. That matches eric's drop. Also seeing many short-running requests causing noisy batches.
maya (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan:
1) Switch autoscaler to manual scale-up + bump pool from 12 -> 20 GPUs (requesting via infra-runbooks). Command: `infra-cli pool resize g-pool-1 --target 20`
2) Roll back the batching change in runtime canary (revert that deploy) to restore `max_batch_latency=10ms` and re-enable `strip_user_id=true` for prefix cache.
3) Increase prefix cache TTL temporarily to reduce misses: `cachectl set prefix_cache.ttl 300s`
4) Throttle non-critical routes (embeddings and low-tier customers) by applying rate-limit rule for 30m: `rlctl apply --route /v1/embeddings --limit 200r/s`
maya (oncall): Executing step 1 now. Pushing resize. infra-cli shows request accepted; cloud provider queueing VM allocation (may be 6-10m). Noting AcmePay (customer_id: acmepay) reporting degraded latency — tess, can you open support ping? @tess
tess (customer-success): Pinged AcmePay POC and flagged we're investigating. They've seen 503s in payment verification flows. They've been moved to 'throttled' fallback as of 08:56 (partial mitigation). I'll keep them updated and request any urgent SLA allowances.
eric (eng-runtime): Preparing rollback of runtime canary. I have the revert PR ready. Plan: cut a hotfix to revert batching heuristic and prefix key change, target 09:05 cut. Expect config flip to propagate within 90s per node.
raj (eng-ml): Quick analysis: the prefix cache key normalization change caused near-zero sharing across sessions for common prefixes because user_id fragment used to be stripped; now keys vary by user and cache hit-rate tanked. Combined with longer max_batch_latency, the batching logic attempted to wait longer but since cache misses produce smaller continuous batches, final batch sizes shrank. TL;DR: cache regress + latency change => throughput collapse.
sophie (eng-sre): Autoscaler: because effective throughput dropped, the autoscaler saw queue growth and attempted scale but cloud quota prevented it. I've initiated a quota increase with cloud provider support (case #CP-9921). Meanwhile manual resize succeeded and new nodes are joining (3/8 up so far).
maya (oncall): Rolling back canary now. `kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deploy/runtime-canary --to-revision=42` -> started. Monitoring logs for prefix_cache.miss_rate and batch_size.
eric (eng-runtime): Hotfix deploy completed at 09:06:10 UTC. Early signals: prefix_cache.miss_rate down to baseline, avg batch size climbing back to ~16 by 09:07. Latency and 5xx trending down.
tess (customer-success): AcmePay reports reduced 503s and their verification latency back to ~normal for a subset of traffic. They've paused their emergency escalation.
sophie (eng-sre): New nodes are healthy. Queue dropped from 25k -> 1.2k over 9 minutes. Autoscaler still constrained but manual size should hold during provider quota increase.
maya (oncall): Current status: mitigated (P1->P2). Root causes prelim: 1) batching/caching regression from canary change (prefix cache key normalization + latency param) 2) autoscaler unable to add capacity due to cloud quota hit -> manual scale required.
maya (oncall): Actions before handoff:
- eric/raj to produce a short postmortem entry with timeline and config diffs (include exact commit and rolling PR).
- sophie to keep cloud quota ticket open and confirm when provider expands limits or we receive final denial.
- I'll create an incident writeup draft and hand off to next oncall at 10:00 UTC.
eric (eng-runtime): I'll open PR to add safer canary gating: require cache hit-rate >= 0.7 on 5m windows before full rollout, and add an automated rollback if avg_batch_size drops >30%.
raj (eng-ml): I'll revert the config in model-serving repo (commit a revert) and add unit tests for prefix key normalization behavior.
sophie (eng-sre): Adding a temporary autoscaler fallback: if scale request returns quota_exceeded, fallback to pre-warmed spare nodes pool before failing. Will circle back with design.
tess (customer-success): I'll send AcmePay a post-incident note summarizing mitigations and ETA for postmortem.
maya (oncall): Handoff: paging next oncall is @jordan at 10:00 UTC. I'll DM the runbook and paste this thread summary. Marking thread as 'mitigated' but keeping channel open until postmortem.
oncall-bot: Incident state updated -> MITIGATED by maya at 09:18 UTC. Incident closed for pages, monitoring continues.
maya (oncall): Brief timeline summary for handoff (to paste into postmortem template):
- 08:30: batching/caching change rolled to canary
- 08:44: prefix_cache.miss_rate spike; avg batch size collapse
- 08:47: queue starts sustained growth
- 08:49: autoscaler attempts scale x3 -> cloud quota errors
- 08:56: manual resizing requested; CS notified AcmePay
- 09:05: rollback cut
- 09:06: hotfix live; metrics recover
- 09:18: queue drained, incident mitigated

maya (oncall): tagging for follow-ups: @eric @raj @sophie to own postmortem and change controls; @product please review risk for customer-facing SLAs. End of thread.
